entities.summary: Domenico Veneziano was an Italian painter of the early Renaissance, active mostly in Perugia and Tuscany. Born around 1398-1400 in Ferrara, Italy, Veneziano was trained in the workshop of Fra Filippo Lippi in Florence. He is best known for his frescoes in the Perugia Cathedral, which include the famous 'Madonna del Fuoco' (1408-1412). Veneziano's work also includes altarpieces, such as the 'Madonna and Child with Saint John the Baptist' (1420s) for the Basilica of San Francesco in Assisi. His paintings are characterized by their use of gold leaf and intricate details, showcasing the influence of Byzantine art. Veneziano died on May 24, 1461, in Florence, leaving behind a legacy as one of the leading artists of the early Renaissance. His work had a profound impact on the development of Western art, influencing artists such as Sandro Botticelli and Domenico Ghirlandaio. The rediscovery of ancient Greek and Roman art during the Renaissance also had a significant impact on Veneziano's work, leading to the creation of more naturalistic and humanistic depictions of the human form.
